<solution_file path="src/solution.py">
import pandas as pd
import csv
import os

# Read the input data
df = pd.read_csv(
    'outputs/t02_eurostat_raw.csv',
    dtype={
        'city_id': str,
        'city_name': str,
        'year': 'int64',
        'indicator_id': str,
        'indicator_name': str,
        'value': 'float64',
        'unit': str
    }
)

# Get the sorted list of all indicator_ids
indicator_ids = sorted(df['indicator_id'].unique().tolist())

# Pivot the long-format data into wide format
# Index: city_id, city_name, year; Columns: indicator_id; Values: value
pivot = df.pivot_table(
    index=['city_id', 'city_name', 'year'],
    columns='indicator_id',
    values='value',
    aggfunc='first'
).reset_index()

# Reorder columns: identifier columns first, then all indicator columns in sorted order
cols = ['city_id', 'city_name', 'year'] + indicator_ids

# Ensure all indicator columns are present (in case some are missing from pivot)
for col in cols:
    if col not in pivot.columns:
        pivot[col] = pd.NA

pivot = pivot[cols]

# Sort by city_id, then year for deterministic ordering
pivot = pivot.sort_values(['city_id', 'year'], na_position='last').reset_index(drop=True)

# Ensure output directory exists
os.makedirs('outputs', exist_ok=True)

# Write CSV with RFC 4180 compliance
# QUOTE_MINIMAL quotes fields containing the delimiter, quote char, or newlines
pivot.to_csv(
    'outputs/t11_city_indicator_matrix.csv',
    index=False,
    quoting=csv.QUOTE_MINIMAL,
    lineterminator='\r\n'
)
</solution_file>
